## Natural history notes

A large wolf spider characterized by a robust brown to dark grayish body, long strong legs, and contrasting pale and dark stripes on the carapace that help it blend into leaf litter, soil, and bark. In Florida, the Georgia Wolf Spider is found in wooded and semi-wooded habitats such as hardwood hammocks, pine flatwoods, forest edges, yards, and areas with logs, leaf litter, and ground cover. It is an active ground predator that hunts insects and other small arthropods without building a capture web, while females carry the egg sac attached to the spinnerets and later carry newly hatched spiderlings on their back.
